 How to Address the City Council
 Any person who would like to address the Council regarding an item on the agenda,
 please fill out a Speaker's Form and submit it to the City Clerk prior to the agenda item
 you would like to discuss. You may address the Council once per meeting, per public
 comment section of the agenda on only those matters within the Council's jurisdiction.
 Please note that you are not required to complete this form or state your name and
 residence in order to speak. Each person addressing the Council is given up to three
 minutes to speak (with double the time allotted to non-English speakers using a
 translator). The amount of time authorized may be adjusted by the chair. If you wish to
 provide information to the Council, please present the City Clerk with 7 copies. Otherwise,
 your materials will simply be added to the administrative record.

 In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, if you require a disability-
 related modification or accommodation to participate in this meeting, please contact the
 City Clerk’s Office at (661) 267-5151 at least 72 hours prior to the meeting.

City Council  Wednesday, April 19, 2023
   City Council Staff Report
DATE:  APRIL 19, 2023
TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL
FROM:  PARKS AND RECREATION DEPARTMENT
DISTRICT:  3
SUBJECT:  APPROVE AGREEMENT NO. A-8314 WITH SMARTE CARTE, INC.
  TO INSTALL LEASED KEYLESS LOCKERS AND SELF-SERVICE
  PAYMENT KIOSKS AT DRYTOWN WATER PARK.

ISSUE
Approve agreement No. A-8314 with Smarte Carte, Inc. to install leased keyless lockers
and self-service payment kiosks at DryTown Water Park.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Award Agreement No. A-8314 with Smarte Carte, Inc. to install leased keyless
  lockers and self-service payment kiosks at DryTown Water Park.
  2. Authorize the City Manager, or her designee, to execute Agreement No. A-8314
  with Smarte Carte, Inc. including minimal and/or non-substantive changes.

BACKGROUND
DryTown Water Park personnel currently manage lockers that are available for customers
to rent. Renting lockers is a common theme park convenience, as renting a locker is not
necessary to utilize and enjoy the park. Approximately 7% of park guests choose to rent
a locker. Operating season 2022, the highest number of lockers rented in a day was 158,
on that day we had 1,993 guests in the park.

Lockers were installed when the park opened in 2006 and are original to the park; lockers
are well beyond their expected lifespan. In anticipation of replacement, staff have
researched replacement options. Through our research, it has been determined that the
existing locker handles are not ADA compliant. Approximately 15% of our inventory can
no longer be repaired, are difficult to operate and their appearance is weathered. Much
of our inventory is routinely out of service during the season, as we work to resolve lost
keys and locker malfunctions.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Award agreement No. A-8314
April 19, 2023
Page 2

Replace with Similar City Owned Keyed System
The current locker system requires a physical key to open and City staff to manage.
Associated challenges include lost keys, keys taken home by mistake, keys found in the
filtration system, or floating in attractions. These challenges lead to the inability to re-rent
lockers, staff assistance to retrieve belongings, and eventual replacement of locking
mechanism or rekey of the mechanism. Replacing with a similar keyed locker system
does not eliminate the current operational challenges associated with keys and would still
require City personnel to continue to manage and maintain the system, resulting in lost
productivity.

Upfront costs include: Purchasing 172 lockers: $80,000; Labor to remove and install the
new lockers are unknown; Annual financials associated with this arrangement include
personnel costs to manage and maintain the system: $12,700; Processing fees: $2,000.

Net revenue based upon current sales trends (7% of total guests) at the current rental
rate ($6) is $18,900 annually. Approximately 4.2 seasons would be required to recover
upfront cost, plus additional seasons for unknown cost to remove and install.

Replace with City Owned Electronic System
An electronic locker system is more convenient for guests, as self-service kiosks issue a
code to unlock. Additional benefits include an easy re-rental process throughout the day
and do not require City personnel to manage. These benefits result in gained staff
productivity, a potential increase in rentals, and improved guest experience.

Upfront costs include: purchasing 172 lockers, and four (4) kiosks, $150,000, labor to
remove and install new lockers are unknown. Annual financials associated with this
arrangement include: service, maintenance and licensing, $15,000 after year one;
processing fees, $2,000.

Net revenue based upon current sales trends (7% of total guests) at the proposed rental
rate range ($8 - $15) is $47,400 annually. Approximately 3.2 seasons would be required
to recover the cost of lockers, plus additional seasons for unknown cost to remove
existing, install and eventually replace the units.

Replace with Leased Electronic System
A leased electronic locker system provides the same benefits as stated above.
Additionally, the lessor is responsible for repairs, service and ultimately replacing units.

Upfront cost is zero. The annual financials associated with this arrangement include:
maintenance and licensing, $0; processing fees, $0.

Net revenue based upon current sales trends (7% of total guests) at proposed rental rate
range ($8 - $15), less 35% vendors share is $41,860 annually. Leasing lockers is
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Award agreement No. A-8314
April 19, 2023
Page 3

approximately 10% less in annual revenue than owning electronic lockers, however, zero
upfront and replacement cost.

DISCUSSION
Based upon associated costs and revenues, it is recommended that leasing lockers is the
most cost-effective approach for the City. To secure a leased electronic locker system,
an RFP was prepared and released on Planet Bids on March 7, 2023. The RFP was sent
to a total of 35 vendors, and as a result, the City received two proposals.

Scoring was based on the following criteria: past performance, qualifications, and
experience, ability to perform the work and meet timelines, references, cost to the City,
and revenue share percentage. The proposal submitted by Smarte Carte, Inc. scored
more points and offered 65% revenue share, compared to 35% from Best Lockers. Their
proposal includes the following services at no cost to the City: installation of 172 keyless
entry lockers and four (4) self-service payment kiosks, easy to use pin code locker access,
PCI compliance, revenue and usage reports, maintenance, repair and replacement parts,
and timely customer support. Smarte Carte, Inc. also has a technician living in Palmdale
who can quickly respond to service requests.

FISCAL IMPACT
There is no expenditure impact associated with this item. Estimated annual net revenue
to the City: $41,860.

STRATEGIC PLAN
Goal II: Ensure long-term fiscal health of the City and maintain funding services.

  A. Manage resources, costs, and liabilities to ensure the City’s long-term fiscal
  health, or
  B. Pursue alternative financing opportunities for continued infrastructure
  improvements and quality community programs.

Goal III: Invest in infrastructure to improve community livability.

  C. Seek innovative, cost effective, customer focused methods of service delivery.

between the City of Palmdale, a public body corporate and politic, (hereinafter called

signatory.

and is qualified to perform the services described in this Contract.

& change making

ISSUE
Approve additional funds of $100,000 for Purchase Order No. 20230000 with Walsma
Oil Company, Inc. for diesel and unleaded fuel, motor oil, and lubricants in an amount
not to exceed $550,000.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve additional funds of $100,000 for Purchase Order No. 20230000 with
  Walsma Oil Company, Inc. for Diesel & Unleaded Fuel, Motor Oil and Lubricants,
  in an amount not to exceed $550,000.

  2. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to authorize Purchase Order No.
  20230000 with Walsma Oil Company, Inc. including non-substantive changes.

BACKGROUND
The City released Invitation for Bid No. 21-004-3300 on March 29, 2021, and awarded
to Walsma Oil Company, Inc. at the June 1, 2021 City Council meeting. In Fiscal Year
2023, Purchase Order 2023000 was issued and approved by the City Council in the
amount of $450,000. As a result of inflationary pressure fuel prices have increased
dramatically this fiscal year, resulting in a shortfall on the current purchase order. Staff
is requesting an additional $100,000, bringing PO 2023000 to a total amount of
$550,000.
DISCUSSION
Maintaining an on-site fueling station and bulk fuel deliveries are important for
accessibility, product security, and best price economics. It is also advantageous in the
event of emergency or disaster situations.

ISSUE
Approve Purchase Order No. 20230495 with Plumber’s Depot for one (1) new GapVax
MC1510-3S4S Combination Jet/Vacuum Truck in an amount not to exceed $604,992.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve Purchase Order No. 20230495 with Plumber’s Depot for one (1) new
  GapVax MC1510-3S4S Combination Jet/Vacuum Truck, in an amount not to
  exceed $604,992.

  2. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to authorize Purchase Order No.
  20230495 with Plumber’s Depot, including non-substantive changes.

BACKGROUND
City Council approved the FY 2023 Mid-Year Budget Adjustments at the March 1, 2023,
meeting. This included a budget adjustment for a second GapVax combination
jet/vacuum truck for the Maintenance Division.

This new GapVax combination jet/vacuum truck will be an addition to the City’s Fleet
assigned to the Sewer Maintenance Department. Due to the California Air Resources
Board’s (CARB) new Clean Fleet Initiative, this vehicle may no longer be available after
January 1, 2024, in California. Purchasing this vehicle ahead of this deadline will provide
the needed time for the technology to improve and allow an equivalent unit to become
available.

The City is utilizing cooperative pricing through Sourcewell Contract No. 101221-GPV
with GapVax, Inc. for the purchase of this vehicle. The vehicle will be purchased from
Plumber’s Depot, who is the exclusive distributor of GapVax Combination Jet/Vacuum
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Approve Purchase Order No. 20230495 with Plumber’s Depot
April 19, 2023
Page 2

Trucks for the lower region of California, including Southern California and the lower
portions of Central California. The truck is currently available to pick up and should be
operational within the next two months.

DISCUSSION
The new GapVax combination jet/vacuum truck will enable the Sewer Division to maintain
two (2) independent cleaning crews to complete scheduled maintenance on the City’s
sewer system. Currently crews maintain around 750,000 linear feet (142 miles) of sewer
mainlines per year and this purchase will allow the division to increase their annual
production rates. Addition of this vehicle will also free up an existing hydro jetter which is
used to prepare sewer lines for CCTV inspection and root abatement, thus increasing
efficiency of both maintenance programs.

Staff recommends that the City Council Approve purchase order 20230495 with
Plumber’s Depot for a second GapVax MC1510-3S4S Combination Jet/Vacuum Truck
in an amount not to exceed $604,992.

FISCAL IMPACT
The purchase order amount for one (1) new GapVax MC1510-3S4S Combination
Jet/Vacuum Truck for FY 2022-2023 will not exceed $604,992. Sufficient funds are
budgeted in Fleet Maintenance Account 15433006-774400.

ISSUE
Approve the First Amendment to the Employment Agreement between the City of
Palmdale and Michael Miller, Assistant City Manager (Agreement No. A-7465).

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve the First Amendment to the Employment Agreement between the City of
  Palmdale and Michael Miller, Assistant City Manager (Agreement No. A-7465).

BACKGROUND
Michael Miller (Employee) was hired by the City of Palmdale on April 16, 1997. He
became the Director of Neighborhood Services on August 26, 2013. On September 6,
2022 he became Interim Assistant City Manager.

This amendment to Mr. Miller’s employment agreement appoints him Assistant City
Manager, thus removing the Interim title.

DISCUSSION
In general, the amendment to the Employment Agreement with Mr. Miller provides for the
following:

  1. The Employee is appointed the Assistant City Manager.

  2. Compensation shall be paid at an annual rate of $264,722.

  3. The Employee is currently enrolled in the California Public Employees’ Retirement
  System (CalPERS) at the 2.7% @ age 55 formula. The Employee shall continue
  to pay the full employee contribution.

  CITY OF PALMDALE

  ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER

DEFINITION

Under administrative direction, assists the City Manager in managing and directing
citywide departmental activities and operations; assists City Manager in providing
administrative guidance to executive staff; relieves the City Manager of day-to-day
duties associated with municipal operations; performs responsible and complex
administrative work; acts for the City Manager in his/her absence.

DISTINGUISHING CHARACTERISTICS

The Assistant City Manager is an administrative management level class, which assists
the City Manager in the overall operations of meeting the City’s established mission and
goals. The incumbent is responsible for the day-to-day coordination and administration
of assigned functions including supervision over assigned departments. The Assistant
City Manager acts for the City Manager in his or her absence. This class is
distinguished from the next higher classification of City Manager, which serves as the
Chief Executive Officer over all City departments and program activities. This is a one
incumbent classification.

SUPERVISION RECEIVED/EXERCISES

Receives administrative direction from the City Manager. Exercises direct and indirect
supervision over assigned areas, including professional, technical and support
personnel.

EXAMPLES OF DUTIES – Duties may include, but are not limited to the following:

Assists and participates in the development and implementation of the City’s strategic
plan and goals and objectives as a result of the strategic plan.

Assists the City Manager in managing and directing the activities of City departments
and in providing administrative guidance to executive staff.

Reviews, interprets, develops, modifies and implements City administrative policies and
their application to specific situations in departments; and resolves conflicts involving
multiple departments in matters/issues not addressed by existing City policies and
procedures.

Manages the coordination and preparation of the budgets, funding mechanisms, and
budget control activities; reviews and approves funding reporting; makes
recommendations to the City Manager on funding opportunities.

  5.1 City Council Strategic Planning Workshop. (Staff Reference: City Manager Perez)

  City Manager Perez went over the agenda for the day and introduced our new Sheriff
  Liaison Jason Hill and Attorney, Colin Burns.

  Attorney Burns presented a PowerPoint presentation on Rules and Decorum. He
  discussed agenda deadlines, who can place items on an agenda and how to agendize an
  item requested by Council.

  Attorney Burns went over Roberts Rules of Order, Rosenberg’s Rules of Order, various
  Parliamentary procedures, and Decorum. Council asked questions regarding the Brown
  Act, public comments, and engaging citizens. Attorney Burns responded.
   City Manager Perez spoke regarding Goal Setting and played a short video “What makes
  life worth living.” She asked everyone to write down one thing that they would like to get
  out of the work session. There was discussion regarding district needs and wants, building
  relationships, roles and responsibilities.

  Councilmembers shared their top priorities, which included film, beautification, green
  space, ownership of Palmdale Boulevard, transportation (Brightline, High Speed Rail),
  regionalism, Public Safety, and the future of the Chimbole Cultural Center. There was
  additional discussion amongst Council regarding alternative power sources, and the
  regional recreation center.

  Councilmember Ohlsen spoke regarding economic opportunity zones. Mayor Bettencourt
  spoke regarding the need for a public Cemetery and Veterans Cemetery. Councilmember
  Bishop shared his thoughts on film, city beautification, illegal dumping and taking over

  Pediatric Trauma Center for Palmdale. Councilmember Loa spoke regarding mental
  health, the resiliency center,

ISSUE
Adopt Resolution No. CC 2023-022, a Resolution of the City Council of the City of
Palmdale approving the Five-Year Public Art Work Plan for projects in the City of
Palmdale in accordance with Chapter 15.01 of the Palmdale Municipal Code.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. CC 2023-022 approving
the Five-Year Public Art Work Plan.

BACKGROUND
The Palmdale City Council approved Resolution No. CC 2020-084, adopted the Public
Art Master Plan, and directed staff to diligently work to implement the recommendations
included in the Public Art Master Plan, one of which is to adopt a work plan annually.
The Commission is required to develop an annual Public Art Work Plan that charts
current and future public art projects and determines resources and funding priorities.
The Five-Year Work Plan strategy will be updated annually to include City-funded
projects, public/private partnerships, maintenance, and a conservation plan. The City
Council will annually approve the Public Art Work Plan proposed by the Commission
and staff.

DISCUSSION
The Public Art Work Plan sets the course for the implementation of all municipal public
art projects, including artwork scope, concept, location, budget, and timeline. The
projected Public Art Fund balance on June 30, 2023, is $799,182. The majority of these
funds were allocated from the City’s General Fund to initiate the program. Currently, the
public art contribution fee assessed to applicable private and municipal projects is not
increasing at the same rate as the program expenses.
